clinician.trajectory_summary: A 34-year-old male farmer presented with one week of bloody diarrhea, constant fever, vomiting, odynophagia, headaches and aches. On admission, physical exam noted fever (39°C), tachycardia, polypnea, no jaundice; digestive exam showed inflamed tonsils with whitish coating and right iliac fossa pain. Labs showed mild thrombocytopenia, neutrophilia, mild liver enzyme elevation, and negative HIV. Initial treatment for severe sepsis was started. On hospital day 3, hemorrhagic signs (melena, conjunctival hemorrhage) and facial puffiness developed, raising suspicion of viral hemorrhagic fever. Risk factor of regular rat consumption was noted. On day 4, patient was isolated, blood sent for Lassa virus RT-PCR testing, and ribavirin therapy started along with vitamin K1, blood transfusions, and oxygen. Patient died on hospital day 6. The RT-PCR test result on 24 January 2018 confirmed Lassa virus infection.
